governing_record: A9.24 items 1, 7, 8, 14; A9.25 message 3 (four classes; parity only on retained physics); docs/rust_migration/PROGRAMME.md section 3 (rules RM-R01..RM-R25)
usage: Copy to docs/rust_migration/contracts/<component_id>/parity_prereg_v1.json (one directory per contract; the report goes next to it as parity_report_v1.json + .md).

Before copying: look the component up in docs/rust_migration/component_inventory_v2.json. Only a component with migration_class ACTIVE_SELECTED_ARCHITECTURE_PHYSICS, or an extract_and_parity_kernel id, may get a contract. A GROUND_REFERENCE_ONLY component needs a recorded requirement of the active test / evidence toolchain first. HISTORICAL_LEGACY_REGRESSION is never contracted; ACTIVE_FLIGHT_INCONSISTENCY only after its resolution, for the corrected successor (RM-R19).
Replace every <...> placeholder and every value marked FILL; delete nothing (a section that does not apply says NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason).
Commit the filled contract ALONE, before any Python-vs-Rust comparison; record its sha256 in docs/rust_migration/migration_state_v1.json (status PREREG_PARITY).
Development comparisons use development_master_seed only and are never scored or reported as a verdict.

A changed reference, tolerance, observable, input set, seed, n or decision rule requires a NEW contract version (v2, v3 ...) with fresh scoring seeds; earlier versions and their reports stay immutable.

component.scope: <whole module | named function subset (kernel granularity, RM-R17) | coupled group: list>
out_of_scope: <functions of the same module not covered; they stay PYTHON_REFERENCE>
component.active_toolchain_requirement: <class G only: the active test / evidence tool that requires it and its record; else NOT_APPLICABLE>
excluded_legacy_paths: <the component's not_ported_parts from the inventory: functions / branches the Rust implementation must NOT reproduce>

contract.registration_statement: Written and committed in its own commit before any Python-vs-Rust comparison of this component was executed. FILL commit after registration in the report, not here.

supersedes.reason: <reference change | code fix after NOT_ADMITTED | contract defect>

reference_implementation.python_commit: FILL (full SHA on the execution branch after the bid freeze: technical source 5eee4b8c82a9403b6bb82d5f8d324526f5d6399b / package b5849affae22a6709ad217a184f6fe896d15410a)
reference_implementation.rule: the campaign refuses to score (REFUSED_REFERENCE_CHANGED) if any reference file sha256 differs from sha256_at_registration; a changed reference requires a new contract version

rust_implementation.rust_commit: FILL at scoring time (recorded in the report build_provenance, not here)
rust_implementation.rule: the report records the sha256 of every provenance source; any later change is UNRECORDED_SOURCE_CHANGE until a scoring execution records it (A9.14 S10.4 RUSTCI-1, generalised)

governing_hashes.rule: both implementations must report these exact values for every run; a mismatch voids the run (status INPUT_MISMATCH, not a verdict)

frozen_data_read_only: <abep_sim/data/... frozen files used; never regenerated (CLAUDE.md rule 1)>

randomized_domain.draw: FILL (one generator per entry point, seeded from campaign_seeds)
randomized_domain.domain_note: numerical parity domain only; not a physics, design or evidence claim

campaign_seeds.derivation: FILL (e.g. numpy.random.SeedSequence([master, entry_index, vector_index]) as parity_prereg_v2)
campaign_seeds.rng_streams: FILL: identical streams (EXACT_STREAM: numpy PCG64 + Generator ported in abep-rng) | different streams (STATISTICAL)
campaign_seeds.development_rule: development comparisons use development_master_seed only and are never scored or reported as a verdict; every execution with scoring_master_seed is appended to campaign_history and the report is committed whatever its verdict

list.name: <observable>
list.tolerance_class: EXACT_BYTES | EXACT_VALUE | ULP_BOUNDED | SOLVER_TOLERANCE | STATISTICAL | EXACT_STREAM

tolerance_classes.EXACT_BYTES: files / serialized outputs byte-identical (sha256 equal); JSON written with the Python-compatible formatter (shortest round-trip float repr, Python exponent form, same indent/separators/key order)
tolerance_classes.EXACT_VALUE: integers, strings, enums, booleans, statuses, error codes, schema shape: equal
tolerance_classes.ULP_BOUNDED: |rust - py| <= k_ulp ulp(py) OR <= r_rel * max(1, |py|); k_ulp and r_rel FILL per observable (proposal k_ulp 4, r_rel 1e-12)
tolerance_classes.SOLVER_TOLERANCE: convergence status EXACT_VALUE; solution |rust - py| <= abs_tol + rel_tol * |py| with abs_tol / rel_tol FILL and tied to the solver's own tolerance; iteration counts reported, not scored
tolerance_classes.STATISTICAL: per test |mean_rust - mean_py| <= z * sqrt(se_py^2 + se_rust^2), z FILL (parity v2: 5.0); zero-se rule |diff| <= 1e-12 * max(1, |mean_py|); aggregate |sum z_i| / sqrt(N) <= FILL (parity v2: 4.0); conditional observables NOT_SCORED below a FILL minimum count
tolerance_classes.EXACT_STREAM: RNG streams identical by construction (ported bit generator and distribution algorithms); then ULP_BOUNDED or EXACT_BYTES as listed per observable

exact_invariants.statement: FILL (partitions, counts, shapes/types, determinism under the same seed in BOTH implementations)

checks.statement: source mass balance closes exactly (CLAUDE.md rule 4)
architecture energy ledger residual < 2 % (absolute comparison for near-zero ledger_resid, as golden check since 2026-09-25)

domain_and_error_parity.mapping_rule: every Python exception class / status used by the component maps to exactly one Rust error variant / status; no Rust path may return a value where Python fails, or fail where Python returns (CLAUDE.md rule 3: no silent fallbacks)

rules: ordering identical where it carries meaning (CSV columns, JSON arrays)
Rust record types generated from or tested against the same schema files

golden_and_reference_cases.rule: references are read as committed; they are never regenerated to make Rust pass (RM-R11); a disagreement is investigated and classified (RUST_DEFECT | PYTHON_REFERENCE_DEFECT (own governance, new contract version) | CONTRACT_DEFECT (new contract version))

captured_reference_outputs.purpose: lets CI check Rust against the Python reference after Python is retired from active execution

julia_bridge.launch_equivalence: argv, environment allow-list and input JSON bytes identical between the Python and Rust launchers (EXACT_BYTES)
julia_bridge.record_comparison: run records EXACT_BYTES for deterministic Julia outputs under identical Julia version / threads / BLAS
julia_bridge.execution_provenance: per-run sidecar: Julia version, HallThruster commit, thread/BLAS env, host, argv, input sha256

performance_measurement.status: reported, not a decision criterion (A9.24 items 1 and 6)

workloads.description: FILL (preferably the matching active workload of PRE_RUST_REFERENCE_BASELINE, docs/performance/pre_rust_reference_baseline_5eee4b8/baseline.json; never a retired workload)

performance_measurement.statistic: median wall-clock and median process CPU per implementation in one session on one machine; speed-up = median_python / median_rust
performance_measurement.machine_manifest: recorded before and after (CPU, RAM, OS, toolchains, thread env)

decision_rules.per_test: every scored observable meets its tolerance class
decision_rules.verdict: ADMITTED iff every per-test, aggregate, invariant, conservation, domain/error and schema check passes and every reference file matches sha256_at_registration
decision_rules.meaning_of_ADMITTED: A9.24 item 1: Rust becomes authoritative for this component (within the registered domain); new production results for it come from Rust and carry implementation = rust, rust_commit and this contract id; the Python component may then be retired from active execution. It is NOT physics validation.
decision_rules.no_retuning: tolerances, observables, inputs, n, seeds and rules are fixed; after NOT_ADMITTED only a code fix plus a new contract version with a fresh scoring_master_seed may follow; the failed report stays; no execution is discarded
decision_rules.disagreement_rule: never rewrite a Python result, golden, fixture or frozen dataset to make Rust pass (RM-R11)
decision_rules.observable_scope: observables are restricted to retained selected-architecture physics; an observable that depends on an excluded legacy path is not registered (RM-R20)

bid_boundary.statement: this contract and its Rust implementation are post-bid-freeze work; no output of it may be cited by the bid package unless the owner re-freezes (PROGRAMME.md section 4; bid_source_guard)

what_this_is_not: not physics evidence or validation: parity shows the Rust code reproduces the Python reference, not that either is right
not a change of any frozen dataset, golden, threshold or requirement
not authority before admission: until ADMITTED the Python reference is authoritative

outputs.runner: abep-parity (Rust) or, while the reference is active, a Python harness that calls the Rust CLI; both record campaign_history

classification_gate.rule: LaB6 / conventional hollow-cathode paths are NOT ported into the active Rust simulator (A9.25 message 3)
checks: component.migration_class is ACTIVE_SELECTED_ARCHITECTURE_PHYSICS, or GROUND_REFERENCE_ONLY with a recorded requirement

no observable, input or code path of the contract belongs to excluded_legacy_paths (LaB6Cathode, lab6_xe, Xe hollow-cathode heater / keeper, C1 flight fallback, hollow-cathode Hall cards, multi-family selection)

if the Python harness must traverse a legacy path to reach the retained kernel (e.g. Config('hall_1stage') for K-GASPATH), the contract states why that path cannot influence the scored observables and registers a check of it (INV-xx)
the Rust implementation contains none of the forbidden identifiers (CI_PLAN.md sec. 1 principle 6) outside the refusal-guard vocabulary
